text:
maria: heads-up deploy-bot alerted on canary for payment-data-plane, autoscaler spike + 503s showing up in canary metrics

deploy-bot: [ALERT] canary: payment-data-plane v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0, health degraded (503 x 18 across 5 pods), reason: nodepool-scale-throttle, action: paused promotion, awaiting manual review
sylvia: looking now, logs show kube-scheduler pending pod binds during burst, HPA bumped from 3->12 but nodepool provider throttled scale ops :/
raj: can we temporarily pin the chart to v2.3.1 for this tenant slice and rollforward fixes later? pin would keep service stable while we debug autoscaler policy
sofia: safe option is pin + revert canary traffic to 0%. but need release notes + notify CS since this affects a small fraction of requests (0.6%)
maria: quick check: are these failures from a values change or chart bump? I can't see image/digest mismatch in logs
sylvia: I grepped canary deploy: values override added connectionPool.maxRequests=500 -> previously 150. That increases concurrency and triggers more pods; combined with HPA target config caused sudden scale. not a chart template issue
raj: ok so values change caused the burst. we have two choices: revert values override in cluster and retry canary, or pin chart & patch values on next CL. what's quickest to get traffic back?
sofia: revert values patch in the canary job and trigger a dry-run then canary dry-promote. command: ``helm upgrade --install payment-data-plane ./charts/payment --namespace prod --set connectionPool.maxRequests=150 --reuse-values --wait --timeout 5m``
sylvia: that should be quick but the provider throttle means new pods might still be pending. we should also reduce HPA max to 6 temporarily to avoid oversubscribe while nodes drain 
maria: deploy-bot, can you re-run the canary with values revert and hold traffic? manual signal ok? :eyes:
deploy-bot: Received manual request by maria at 1768001301. Running: ``helm upgrade --namespace prod payment-data-plane ./charts/payment --set connectionPool.maxRequests=150 --wait``. Canary traffic set to 0%. Will post status updates.
sofia: I'll draft a one-line release note: "Temporarily revert connectionPool increase in canary due to provider-scale throttling; follow-up patch to re-evaluate HPA/NodePool config." cc @support-team
raj: also add a short checklist so we don't reintroduce this: 1) perf eval for connectionPool with representative load 2) HPA target tuning 3) nodepool scale policy review
sylvia: deploy-bot update: canary pods are back to Running but there are 2 pod restarts from init timeout, logs show kubelet image pull cached ok. health checks passing now
maria: good. status?
deploy-bot: promotion paused. Canary health = green (0 errors over 7m). traffic remains 0%. Pin decision pending manual approval.
sofia: propose we do NOT pin chart version; this was values-driven. instead we'll merge a hotfix to the values override repo and run a controlled canary later. anyone object?
raj: +1. no pin. but add a guard in deploy pipeline to block values overrides that increase concurrency > 2x without perf eval.
sylvia: I'll open a PR: "revert-connpool-canary-hotfix" and tag infra to review autoscaler defaults.
maria: I'll send a short note to #release-ops and CS: brief incident + rollback of values in canary, expected no user impact. sofia can you add that note to release notes draft?
sofia: done, pushed to draft release-notes/wip. linking here: https://git.internal/release-notes/1387
maria: thanks. closing thread once deploy-bot confirms promotion stays paused for 30m and metrics look stable
deploy-bot: manual hold confirmed until 1768003034. will auto-unpause if any manual override happens. :white_check_mark:
sofia: follow-up tickets: INFRA-998 (nodepool autoscale policy review), REL-1203 (values override guard), QA-551 (connpool perf test). I'll assign after PR lands.
raj: nice work team. quick win. :thumbsup:
